findings.summary: Worker-side rendering preserved the modest p 50 gain. Rendering and OCR now overlap and account for 93.9% of call time; embedding is 5.2%.
observations: Three ordinary calls had a 2.237 s median. The additional instrumented call passed exact OCR/chunk and frozen-vector checks.
NACA pages 1,2,3 rendered in three existing page workers in about 35,44,43 ms in the first measured call. No rendered images were transferred through the parent.
Seven one-second samples per GPU showed mean busy levels 80.6%,74.7%,68.7%,82.3%. These activity readings do not establish peak-compute saturation.
Each GPU recorded 2,336 fixed 32-row decoder matrix launches in 32 instrumented engine iterations. Narrow output/down projections used two row tiles in 99 of 128 sampled iterations across GPUs.
At the eight-request limit, four draft tokens plus one verification token can produce 40 rows; three drafts produce 32. A three-draft trial can test whether avoiding the second row tile helps.
The separate two/eight-draft trials preceded fixed 32-row decoder tuning. Their results do not test this newly introduced tile boundary; any new trial must retain exact frozen outputs.
findings.next_step: Compare three GPU n-gram draft tokens with a fresh four-token control on the retained worker-rendering configuration. Check all three evaluator metrics, especially the Census tail.
findings.optimization: Keep lookup lengths 2–5, fixed 32-row tiles, concurrency 8, four-GPU embeddings, rendering placement, dataset and references constant. Profile actual kernel grids before attributing a gain to reduced padding.
